title: stride-aware-kv-compactor-and-head-tiling-optimizations
author: Ava Chen
description:
Motivation: Several MQA/GQA model families (notably private Llama forks and Qwen-family variants used in internal benchmarks) show pathological KV cache fragmentation and uneven head-wise compute when switching between short and long contexts. This PR introduces a stride-aware KV compactor plus a head-tiling hint path that reduces memory churn, improves kernel utilization for multi-query attention, and unlocks more effective continuous batching for mixed-token workloads.

What changed (summary): Implemented a compacting pass that coalesces sparsely populated KV slabs based on observed token stride rather than strict contiguous offsets; added a lightweight per-model head-tiling hint that informs the kernel selector about preferred head-groupings for MQA/GQA variants; extended the continuous-batching scheduler to prefer requests with compatible head-tiling hints and to trigger compaction opportunistically during low-load windows.

Why this is safe: Compaction is run as an in-place, reversible operation with a small bitmap guard and a conservative verification step that falls back to the previous layout if checksums mismatch. The head-tiling hint is advisory only — runtimes without the hint still use existing behavior. All changes include unit tests and a guarded feature flag (runtime.enable_stride_compactor) turned off by default for earlier deploys.

Benchmark summary: On internal perf-lab (A100 x8): MQA-8 models showed 18% higher sustained throughput and 12% p99 latency reduction for 512->2048 token mixes. GQA-style models improved throughput by ~9% due to better kernel packing. Llama-2-13B repro with model quirks dataset shows median token cost down ~8% when compactor is enabled. End-to-end regressions run against our standard CI evals show no statistical quality degradation across our prompt suite.

Rollout plan: feature flag gated, staged canary for 5% of traffic on dedicated clusters, monitor token-level latency, KV cache fragmentation metric, and per-model kernel selection distribution. If fragmentation increases or p99 regresses >10% on canaries, automatic rollback via the control-plane rollout policy is configured.

Related Linear/Jira: ENG-4821, ENG-5910.

Notes for reviewers: focus attention on compactor correctness checks, kernel-hint API shape in tiling.h, and scheduler heuristic probabilities in continuous_batching.cpp. I included a micro-benchmark harness under tests/perf/ that reproduces the regressions we observed in the field.

ci_checks: perf-regressions - initial fail (p99 flakiness), rerun -> passed (14m)
review_comments: Priya Singh: Large change—can you outline the invariants the compactor preserves? I want to ensure we won't break streaming checkpoints.

Ava Chen: The compactor keeps per-slab sequence ids and an in-place remap table; we verify checksums and restore the prior layout if the verification fails. Added a diagram in the code comments and an extra unit test for streaming checkpoint restore.

Diego Morales: Head-tiling hint looks sensible, but can we avoid adding another model-specific switch in kernel selector? Suggest exposing a small enum and a heuristic weight rather than bespoke branching.
Ava Chen: Reworked selector to use a hint enum + a score multiplier. That simplified the hot path and reduced branching in the kernel loop.
Liam O'Connor: Observed perf test flakiness on perf-regressions; failure was due to non-deterministic eviction timing. You added a guard—looks good. Approving after CI green.
Priya Singh: Approved after verifying the compaction rollback test cases and rollout doc.
merge_outcome: merged after CI green and 3 approvals
release_notes: Introduces a stride-aware KV compactor (feature-flagged) and an advisory head-tiling hint to improve kernel packing for MQA/GQA models. Expected improvements: lower p99 latency and higher throughput for mixed-context workloads. Rollout gated by runtime.enable_stride_compactor.
